context: Follow-up pass to the 2026-07-03 attribution audit, targeting the remaining class of 'Public record: ...' source_refs on Phase 2.3 deep-research atoms — prediction/timeline claims (FSD coast-to-coast, robotaxis, Mars architecture, Roadster, Model 3 ramp, Cybertruck, human-on-Mars) whose citations name specific real-world events (Tesla Autonomy Day 2019, IAC Guadalajara 2016, TED 2022, WSJ 2011, etc.) that were LLM-guessed rather than drawn from corpus content. 9 suspect atoms out of 874 were scanned and adjudicated against the local transcript corpus; each was either verified, reattributed to a corpus source that verifiably contains the claim in Elon's own diarized words, stripped of its unsupported citation, or left as documented residue where corpus support is only partial (split multi-claim atoms whose compiled specifics no single source can carry).
method: Three-stage process mirroring the 2026-07-03 audit: (1) scan of all 874 elon_musk_atoms for suspect 'Public record'-style refs and event-named citations not present in source/sources.json, yielding 9 suspects; (2) xhigh-effort adjudication of each suspect against the local corpus (source/transcripts/*.json, diarized, EM-labeled speaker turns), searching for the atom's specific claims, quoted lines, dates, and figures — reattribution only where the transcript verifiably contains the claim in Elon's own words, never where the match is a different claim, an interviewer's line, or would launder a fabricated quote onto a real source; (3) adversarial refuter pass challenging each proposed KEEP/REATTR verdict, demoting partial matches with factual mismatches or uncorroborated endpoints to residue rather than reattributing as-is; plus (4) public-record date verification for reattribution targets — new source_dates come from verified publication dates (date_corrections map), never LLM guesses, and bogus guessed dates are nulled rather than replaced.
